thread:
maria: Heads-up — ran terraform apply on cluster-eu-west-1-gpu last night and hit a CNI managed-addon mismatch. Two nodegroups upgraded fine, third (ng-gpu-prod-3) never finished rolling and several GPU pods got stuck in CrashLoopBackOff / Evicted. Terraform shows the addon at v1.9, nodes report v1.8 in annotations. Anyone seen this pattern?

deploy-bot: terraform apply started by @maria — plan: 6 to add, 2 to change, 0 to destroy

maria: snippet from one of the stuck nodes: ```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "ng-gpu-prod-3|NotReady"
ip-10-0-3-45   NotReady   3d   v1.28.4-eks-abc   192.168.10.45   <none>   <none>
```

maria: and node describe shows CNI version annotation still v1.8: ```
Annotations:
  eks.amazonaws.com/addons: cni:v1.8
  cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/cni-version: v1.8
```

ashok: do we manage CNI through the EKS managed-addon or a helm chart on this cluster? If managed-addon, AWS console sometimes forces an update and terraform state drifts. Which terraform resource is for this addon?

maria: it's the EKS managed addon (aws_eks_addon.cni) in infra/gpu/cluster.tf. We saw an operator-triggered update in CloudTrail at 2025-10-11T22:14Z — looks like someone clicked upgrade in the console for another cluster and it kicked off a region-wide rollout. Terraform applied v1.9 but the daemonset on these custom GPU AMIs didn't get the new image because the AMI has a pinned CNI binary.

liam: Oof. So the addon version and node binary mismatch. For GPU AMIs we usually bake a pinned CNI for performance/stability. If the managed addon upgraded control-plane bits but nodes still have old binary, kubelet/CNI handshake will break during pod lifecycle and image pulls. Options: 1) replace nodegroup (create_new -> drain -> terminate) 2) patch AMI or 3) roll back addon to v1.8. 3 is faster but not ideal long-term.

ashok: I vote for a controlled node replacement for ng-gpu-prod-3 using create_before_destroy and a canary nodegroup. We should avoid rolling back addon globally. Can we do in Terraform safely? Create a new ng-gpu-prod-3b with same launch template but updated AMI that has v1.9, then migrate pods and decommission old group.

maria: agreed. Quick notes: current ASG for ng-gpu-prod-3 has 8 nodes (spot preferred). If we create new on-demand canary nodes it will fall back to on-demand for ~10-15 min while pods migrate — cost spike estimate: roughly $120/hr extra during migration window, ~$(estimated)2.8k/month if we run frequent replacements. This is urgent so short-term cost is acceptable.

liam: I'll prepare a terraform patch: add node_group_ng_gpu_prod_3b with lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true } and set max_unavailable=1 on the rollout pipeline. Also add a backend check that the AMI contains the CNI v1.9 binary. Preflight script suggestion: ```bash
# preflight to run in pipeline
ssh -i /tmp/key ec2-user@${AMI_INSTANCE} 'cat /opt/cni/bin/cni-plugin | grep "v1.9" || exit 1'
kubectl get daemonset aws-node -n kube-system -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}' | grep v1.9
```

ashok: good. Also add a GitOps guard in the pipeline: if terraform plan changes managed-addon.version, require manual approval. Prevent accidental console upgrades from diverging state next time.

maria: +1 on manual approval. I'll open an infra PR to: bump AMI for gpu-ami->2025.10.09-v2 (contains cni v1.9), add the canary nodegroup, and gate addon version changes behind an approval step in CI.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2025-2415 — cluster-eu-west-1 gpu nodegroup drift affecting pods. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2025-2415

liam: I'll run the canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC. I'll also add a small smoke test in the rollout that runs a GPU inference container (simple identity model) to ensure pods schedule and initialize.

maria: thanks — tagging @ashok and @liam. I'll draft the PR and add the approval step to the GitHub Actions pipeline. Plan to run canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC; will post results here. :thumbsup:
